assertion_audit: tests/test_display_flux.py:269 asserts the reproduction relative error under 1e-10; dropping a moment column or contracting in the wrong order reddens it, and logs/negative-control.log shows it red at 2.53e-2 under a swapped column.

tests/test_display_flux.py:265-268 compares display.max_node_mismatch_wb against a residual the test computed through operator.raster_image, a different implementation from the builder's FluxTarget path at display_flux.py:119-136, so a wrong operand in either path reddens it; logs/control-mismatch.log shows it red when the report is zeroed.

tests/test_display_flux.py:383-386 assert the branch dict's key set, well-formedness and the one-lobe/two-leg counts; replacing the builder's assembly with an empty dict reddens them (logs/control-branches.log), and they would also catch a level so wrong that the assembly degenerates.

tests/test_display_flux.py:394-397 compares every branch array to a direct assemble_separatrix_branches call, but passes display.saddle_flux, display.flux, display.radius and display.height into that call, so the comparison pins the field and grid arguments and not the level: a builder that assembled at the lattice saddle's value would satisfy it.
tests/test_display_flux.py:460-464 assert the refusal on an O-point seed; restoring the fail-open fallback in display_flux.py:166-176 reddens them.
tests/test_display_flux.py:423 asserts the saddle lies within 20 mm of the seed the test supplied at :419, so it cannot distinguish a polished saddle from an unchanged seed.

evidence.added_failure_source: The reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite or after_suite block, so added_failure_count is derived from the only post-change arm on record, logs/gate-fail-closed.log, which reports 7 passed and EXIT=0 and therefore carries no failing ids.

findings.text: The reference assembly is called with display.saddle_flux, the builder's own output, so both sides of the equality at :395 move together on the level; a regression that assembled the separatrix at the lattice saddle's level or at the axis value instead of the map's polished saddle would leave every assertion in the test green, and the commit message's claim that a wrong level is visible to the gate is not borne out.

xpoint_rz is [DIVERTED_CENTRE, 0.0] at :419 and the assertion accepts a saddle within 20 mm of that same point, so the test also passes if the polish never moves the seed; only tests/test_display_flux.py:460-464 distinguishes a real polish from a returned seed, and it exercises the extremum path rather than the saddle path.

_diverted_field re-implements the diverted-null configuration already defined at tests/test_separatrix_branches.py:29 instead of importing or parameterising that owner, so the two fixtures can drift and the fragment's claim that it is the same null configuration the branch assembler's tests use holds only for this copy.

The lattice saddle's convergence flag is discarded, so a lattice polish that fails yields lattice_saddle_rz NaN and saddle_offset_mm NaN while saddle_converged reads True, and a panel reporting the offset would report NaN with no signal that the lattice read failed.
